The normal accrual is not zero: depreciation reduces earnings without leaving cash, and each sector has its own working capital cycle. That's why the benchmark is the distance to the sector median in the same period (Dechow and Sloan sector model, ⟨0⟩, tested in Dechow, Sloan and Sweeney, ⟨1⟩), in absolute value: earnings far above cash and far below cash count the same, because a very negative accrual can be a write-off or a provision that releases earnings later (big bath). A deviation below ⟨2⟩ is high quality; from ⟨3⟩ to ⟨4⟩, moderate; from ⟨5⟩ on, low. The median uses companies with complete data; a sector with fewer than ⟨6⟩ of them uses the full sample's median. The alert level combines this reading with the M-Score.

Reading: the Critical level and the capital signals (ICA, BPM) separate stress well. The provision (IPR) doesn't anticipate stress, but does anticipate an earnings drop, which is what it measures; the non-recurring item (VRN) anticipates both, with few cases. That's why two or more earnings signals become "Earnings to check," not a risk level. Coverage, growth, and problem assets barely separate.
